summary.intent: Plan and execute GSD phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) end-to-end in cipher-box — research, scope decisions, plan generation, verification, and wave-based execution — while also spinning up an independent worktree to start phase 69 in parallel.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed (research, VALIDATION.md, D-07 full-boundary scope decision, pattern mapping, REQUIREMENTS registration, 12 plans/7 waves, plan-checker PASSED). Execution proceeded sequentially through Waves 1–6 (11/12 plans) with spot-checks catching and fixing premature requirement-completion markings and a planner coverage gap (unowned component/importer residuals); a phase-69 worktree was created off origin/main for parallel work; Wave 7 (final plan, mirror revert) was dispatched but not yet confirmed complete when the transcript ends.

repo: gsd-tools commit helper produces false-negative 'commit_failed' reports even when the commit actually lands — must verify via `git log` rather than trusting the reported status.

SDK-READ-0X requirements in REQUIREMENTS.md must stay unchecked until the corresponding legacy web service is actually deleted (Wave 6/plan 11) — multiple early executors (plans 01, 02, 05) prematurely marked them [x] and had to be reverted.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel plan execution is expensive (each worktree needs its own `pnpm install`) and not worth it when most waves are single-plan — sequential execution on the main tree is equally correct when same-wave plans are file-disjoint.

D-07 apps/web/src boundary grep gate has known false-positive classes: inline `type`-only imports and matches inside files that are themselves scheduled for deletion — both must be filtered out manually when auditing.

Planner-generated plans can leave 'unowned' consumer files (components/hooks that read data types governed by the phase but aren't assigned to any plan) — these surface as residual importers blocking later deletion plans and require a manual grep audit before the deletion plan runs.
git fetch fails from this sandboxed session (no GitHub network access); local origin/main ref must be relied on and cross-checked for currency (e.g. against the fork-base of another recent branch).

enforceResolved gate added to dfsFindFolder child loop by plan 68.2-01

resolveChildren docstring documents intentional per-child skip-on-failure: target folder is already gated before this runs, so an unverifiable sibling is omitted rather than rendered with stale/attacker content — trust boundary preserved even though 4 test assertions changed

workflow: During wave-based execute-phase, independently re-run acceptance/security tests after each executor completes rather than trusting the subagent's self-reported pass, especially for security-critical waves (ROT-07 gate, D-07 boundary grep).
Before dispatching parallel worktree executors, verify worktree.baseRef (head vs fresh/origin) — forking from origin/main instead of HEAD would silently drop all newly-committed PLAN.md files.

When scheduling a wake-up (ScheduleWakeup) after a delay, recompute the current time immediately before the call — a delay computed earlier and reused after an interruption (e.g. quota reset) fires late.
A stray/duplicate scheduled wakeup that can't be cleanly retracted is not harmful if the resuming session can recognize the work is already in flight and treat the wake as a no-op.

friction: gsd-tools commit helper repeatedly reported false-negative 'commit_failed' across multiple commits, requiring manual git log verification each time.
